Data privacy is a critical consideration in the reporting of healthcare and clinical database metrics, particularly when dealing with small patient cohorts. In the context of the [[akut-kirurgi-databasen|Akut Kirurgi Databasen]], strict discretion rules are applied to published indicator results to protect patient anonymity. Specifically, when indicator results contain only one or two patients (n = 1 or n = 2) in either the numerator or the denominator, the data is removed from the public annual report published on www.sundhed.dk [^src1]. To maintain transparency about the redacted data, these suppressed results are replaced with a hash symbol (#) alongside an explanatory note [^src1]. The standard explanation provided in the report explicitly states that the result has been removed for discretion reasons because there are only one or two patients or care pathways in the numerator or denominator [^src1]. These measures ensure that individual patient identities cannot be inferred from publicly available statistical reports.

## Claims

- Indikatorresultater, hvor der kun optræder n = 1 eller n = 2 i enten tæller eller nævner, vil af diskretionshensyn blive fjernet og erstattet med # samt en forklaringsnote i den offentliggjorte årsrapport på www.sundhed.dk [^src1] (akut-kirurgi-databasen)
  Type: data-privacy
  Page: 86
  Source: wikis/rkkp-akdb/raw/AKDB_2024.pdf, pages 86-90
- Forklaringsnoten lyder: ”Resultatet er af diskretionshensyn fjernet, da der er et eller to patienter/forløb i tæller eller nævner” [^src1] (akut-kirurgi-databasen)
  Type: data-privacy
